clue.text: Retired Arab acquires first coffee maker

indicators.note: someone retired has gone back, so the word is read in the backward direction
to acquire is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
1st, written out as the abbreviation IST

explanation.surface: A retired Arab gentleman takes up a new hobby: making coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: BARA holds IST to give BARISTA; 'first' is shortened to 1ST, read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is the person in a café who prepares espresso drinks for customers.

clue.text: Producer of spray for treating moist ear

indicators.note: treating something works it over and changes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that sprays liquid, recommended for an ear that is too moist.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: Succeeded to leave Italian lady nudist exhausted in the dark

indicators.note: the abbreviation for succeeded departs from the following word, removing it
an exhausted word is emptied out, keeping only its two ends

blocks.note: s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies; it is removed

explanation.surface: An Italian woman leaves a nudist beach worn out, with no idea of something.
explanation.walkthrough: s. is the genealogists' abbreviation for succeeded; a signora is an Italian married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kept in the dark is to be uninformed, so someone in the dark lacks knowledge.

clue.text: Ground reports of dread more solid

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said out loud

blocks.note: dread is terror, which in some accents is said like this
more solid is firmer, said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: News reports about a dread that is growing ever more solid.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech TERROR FIRMER and TERRA FIRMA are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for dry land, the solid ground under one's feet as opposed to sea or air.

clue.text: Authority to travel island within very small area

indicators.note: within means placed inside the following pair of letters

blocks.note: a, the short form of area

explanation.surface: Permission is needed to visit a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' just marks area as shortened to its initial; the island sits between the two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is the official endorsement in a passport permitting entry to a country.

clue.text: Ran and met high ball crossed into box?

definitions.text: met high ball crossed into box

blocks.note: first meaning: led or was in charge of, as of a company

blocks.clueFragment: met high ball crossed into box
blocks.note: second meaning: in football, struck the ball with the forehead after a cross

explanation.surface: A footballer sprinted and nodded a cross into the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is the penalty area in football; a cross is a ball played in from the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: To head something is both to lead it and, in football, to hit the ball with one's forehead.

clue.text: Serving up tabbouleh canapés, filled with style

indicators.note: the phrase is filled with the letters, which sit inside its run of words
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters read backwards across the two words

explanation.surface: A caterer serves Middle Eastern salad on canapés with real flair.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'h canapés' backwards gives the answer; tabbouleh is a parsley and bulgur salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and stylishness in how someone does things.

clue.text: Flatbread in English pub, it's prepared for late customers

indicators.note: in places the bread inside the letters around it

blocks.note: a flat Middle Eastern bread, also spelt pitta
PH, the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A pub serving English flatbread prepares food for its late-night drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not out after hours: the customers are the departed.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription composed for a dead person's tombstone, so it is prepared for the deceased.

clue.text: Sacked politician admits a dangerous leak

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the politician takes the article inside

explanation.surface: A dismissed MP confesses to a damaging leak of information.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRED is followed by MP holding A. The leak is not of secrets but of gas from a coal seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is methane seeping into coal mines, where it can explode.

clue.text: Establish boundaries for Rugby ironworks

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its two edges, so only those letters count

blocks.note: to set up, as a business

explanation.surface: Setting the touchlines for a game of rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is also a town in England, which suits a works.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundry is a factory where metal such as iron is melted and cast into shapes.

clue.text: Pass time chasing vehicle, one on the highway to hell?

definitions.text: one on the highway to hell?

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the time letter follows the vehicle

explanation.surface: A driver passes the time chasing another car down a road to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' puts T after CAR. The definition plays on the idiom 'going to hell in a handcart', meaning heading for disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of going to hell in a handcart makes this small pushed barrow the vehicle of ruin.

clue.text: Spooner's unfurnished vestibules – they'll upset the cat

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of two words

blocks.note: empty entrance rooms; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Empty entrance halls that a cat would find unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat grooming itself swallows fur that clumps in its stomach until it is sick, so these balls of fur upset it.

clue.text: Topless, Carrie's on the move in mountain range

indicators.note: without a top, the word loses its first letter
letters on the move change places with one another

blocks.note: read as one word, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Carrie sunbathes topless while trekking through the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: CARRIES loses its C, and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, a word from Spanish meaning saw.

clue.text: China's joint alliance

blocks.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a friend's

explanation.surface: A joint venture between China and another nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendship is a bond of mutual goodwill, like an alliance between two people.

clue.text: New lip oil has developed into a handy accessory

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so these letters take a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A new lip oil product has become a convenient beauty item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' is part of the fodder as well as the indicator phrase: N, LIP OIL and HAS together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail polish is applied to fingernails, so it is an accessory worn on the hand.

clue.text: Director deleting content of Lawrence article

indicators.note: with its contents removed, only the shell of the name is left

explanation.surface: A film director edits material about Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lean directed Lawrence of Arabia, which makes the surface fit.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lean was the British film director of Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: Teenage hoodlum initially committing theft, having a pound?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two preceding words

explanation.surface: A young thug is caught stealing, hoping to get a quid out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound looks like money; here it is a beating pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something throbbing beats with a strong pulse, so it has a pounding rhythm.

clue.text: Plucky husband in very western TV programme

indicators.note: in puts the husband inside the word for very

explanation.surface: A brave husband stars in a cowboy series on television.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside SO, then W follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A game show is a television programme in which contestants compete for prizes.

clue.text: Lug around witch last seen in village somewhere near Tunis

indicators.note: what is seen last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to cart something is to carry it laboriously
an ugly old woman, a witch

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a witch round a village in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' belongs with 'Lug', not as a signal to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient Phoenician city whose ruins now lie in the suburbs of Tunis.

clue.text: School day came, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A pupil laments that the first day of term arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a type of school, in Britain a state school run independently of the local council.

clue.text: Issue number one: tide is turning

indicators.note: turning round makes the whole string run the other way

explanation.surface: The first issue of a magazine reports that the tide is changing.
explanation.walkthrough: NO, I and TIDE are joined and then the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper or magazine, all copies printed at one time.

clue.text: Open top of anchovy container

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to open the lid on a pot of anchovies.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is ajar is slightly open, neither closed nor fully opened.

clue.text: Policeman claiming old laws to be scrapped? Utter tosh

indicators.note: laws that are scrapped are broken up, so the letters are jumbled
to claim is to take hold of, so the policeman holds the jumble inside

blocks.note: informal word for a police officer
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A policeman says outdated laws should be abolished, which a listener calls rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: COP is split to hold the rearranged letters: CO + DSWALLO + P.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense, the same idea as utter rubbish.

clue.text: Wife attacked case of Burgundy and port

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters count

explanation.surface: A wife set about a crate of Burgundy and some port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgundy and port look like wines; port is a harbour town. Whitby is a fishing port on the Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitby is a seaside harbour town in North Yorkshire, England, known for Dracula and its abbey.

clue.text: Homer tacitly accepting a vow of silence

indicators.note: the phrase accepts the letters into itself, holding them within its run

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Homer quietly agrees to keep his mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacitly' sits nicely with the definition: tacit means unspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's code of silence, forbidding members to talk to the police.

clue.text: Editor busily cutting old, odd bits of Truss rubbish

indicators.note: busily suggests bustling activity, so the letters are moved around
cutting removes something, here the letter for old
odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters

blocks.note: standard abbreviation; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: An editor hurriedly trims bits of a story about former PM Liz Truss as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion happens before the shuffle. Liz Truss was a short-lived British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste matter left over, so it amounts to rubbish.

clue.text: State University starts to teach ancient history

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A state university begins to offer courses in ancient history.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the American West.

clue.text: Know-all Joe put back in detention by British school leader

indicators.note: putting back sends the word in the opposite direction
detention holds someone in, so the soldier is kept between the other pieces

explanation.surface: A smart-alec pupil called Joe is given detention by a British headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: GI Joe is the generic American soldier, so Joe alone stands for GI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bighead is a conceited person who thinks they know everything, much like a know-all.

clue.text: Bare your bottom and smile, Ray!

blocks.note: to moon is to show one's buttocks as a prank

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to someone called Ray to flash his backside and grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a name being addressed; it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonbeam is a shaft of moonlight, one ray of light from the moon.

clue.text: More difficult when – hic! – we're drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters lurch out of order

explanation.surface: Hiccupping drinkers find everything harder once they are drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewier food is tougher to eat, taking more effort to bite through, so harder going.
